documentation.rationale: The identity half is present: VIN, window sticker copy, clean Carfax claim and a title in the seller's name. The maintenance half is only asserted. 'Service records' are listed but not shown, and there is no IMS, cooling or scan evidence.

condition.rationale: Photos show a clean black exterior with PPF, factory wheels without visible rash, matching Pilot Sport 4S tires with good tread, and clean Stone Gray seats. Nothing is stated wrong. Engine bay, underside, tire dates and cylinder condition are unproven.

price_value.rationale: The current bid ($987) is only an opening figure. The likely hammer for a 21k-mile manual S sits around the fair value band ($25,837–$35,452). No known-work items are established, but there is no IMS retrofit, which is a potential $3.5k line.

mission_fit.rationale: It is a manual mid-engine roadster with a strong point of view and good resale. However, the M97 3.4 carries bore-scoring and IMS exposure that cuts against a 'reliable bridge'. The likely hammer also sits above the $10,000–$19,000 ideal band.

logistics.rationale: Prescott, AZ is a fly-and-drive distance to Carmel. A remote BaT auction requires arranging a PPI before the close. Porsche-capable shops exist regionally, but seller access is unconfirmed. CA registration is likely feasible but unverified.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: S model, six-speed manual, documented low mileage, 19in SportDesign wheels, Stone Gray interior and window sticker. Black paint is common, and PASM and Sport Chrono are not stated.

ppi_focus: Borescope all six cylinders, with attention to the thrust side of the bank 2 bores, for scoring
Durametric scan for fault memory, cam deviation values and over-rev counts
Cold-start listen for piston slap, chain or variocam rattle, and AOS smoke
Oil filter cut and inspection for metallic debris
IMS area and rear main seal for weeping at the bellhousing; clutch engagement point and DMF judder
Coolant expansion tank, water pump weep hole and coolant crust under the rear
Front radiators and condensers for debris packing and corrosion
Convertible top cycling, cables and drive blocks, hydraulic leaks onto trunk carpet, and drain and footwell dryness
Front control arms, coffin arm bushings, top mounts and tie rods
Tire date codes and the CA smog-relevant emissions label
what_would_change_verdict: A clean borescope and Durametric scan with no over-revs would materially de-risk the M97
Records showing IMS retrofit or recent cooling-system service would raise documentation and condition
Any scoring, metal in the filter, or out-of-spec cam deviation would move it sharply down
Refusal of a pre-close PPI would leave this as a remote auction with engine risk unaddressed
A hammer price landing well inside the budget would improve price value and mission fit
evidence.mission_note: It meets the manual, point-of-view and resale parts of the enthusiast-bridge brief. The 987.1 M97 engine risk and a likely hammer above the ideal band cut against the reliable, low-all-in bridge goal unless a borescope and records clear it.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes identity well: the VIN decodes cleanly to a 2007 Boxster S 3.4, and a window sticker, a clean Carfax claim and a seller-named Arizona title are included. Photos show a clean, stock black car with PPF, factory 19in wheels, matching Pilot Sport 4S tires and tidy Stone Gray seats, with no defects observed. Nothing in the listing documents the model-critical items: no IMS evidence, no borescope, no scan, no cooling-system receipts and no top/drain evidence. The 'service records' are asserted but not shown. The mileage pattern (about 4k miles in the first nine years) means age-related rubber, cooling and seal items carry more weight than the 21k odometer implies. The current $987 bid is an opening figure, and comparable low-mile manual S sales point to a hammer within the fair-value band. PPI access and reserve status are open questions.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller through BaT before November 3 requesting the engine number, scans of all service records, tire date codes, a cold-start video, and permission for a pre-close PPI with borescope at a Porsche-specialist shop in the Prescott/Phoenix area.
